(Today through Thursday)...
Issued at 254 AM EDT Fri Sep 11 2026

The front that brought the showers on Thursday is now south of 
the Ohio River and will wash out today. Remnant moisture associated 
with the front will interact with a weak upper low to produce 
additional chances for rain across the Ohio Valley late today into 
Saturday.

Upper ridging will expand north into the region late weekend into 
early next week with warmer temperatures returning through the 
middle of next week. A cold front will become nearly stationary 
across the lower Great Lakes next week before gradually sliding into 
the Ohio Valley during the second half of next week with increasing 
chances for showers and thunderstorms.

Today through Saturday Night

Skies continue to clear slowly from the north early this morning as 
high pressure resides over the Great Lakes. The cold front from 
Thursday has now shifted into the Tennessee and lower Ohio Valleys 
with convection south of the Ohio River. 06Z temperatures ranged 
from the mid 60s to the low 70s.

Much of the day will be dry as the region sits under the influence 
of the aforementioned high pressure to the north. The deeper 
moisture associated with the front remains in relatively close 
proximity to the south and this will keep clouds in greater 
abundance across the southern half of the forecast area today. As 
the boundary washes out and a weak upper low develops over the 
Ozarks...the moisture axis will be drawn back north into the 
southern part of the forecast area late day as the high shifts east 
into New England. Instability is weak but cannot entirely rule out a 
few showers or rumbles of thunder developing across the lower Wabash 
Valley east into far southern portions of central Indiana into this 
evening prior to the loss of heating.

The upper low will weaken into an open wave as it pivots to the 
northeast into the Ohio Valley overnight. Expect an increase in 
coverage in showers during the predawn hours focused particularly 
over the southeast half of the forecast area. The wave aloft will 
drift east across the area on Saturday with scattered showers and 
storms in a moist and unstable airmass. The upper wave axis and 
deeper moisture plume will shift east of the region by late day with 
a downtick in convective coverage from the west as the afternoon 
progresses. Weak surface ridging builds in Saturday night with dry 
yet muggy conditions.

Temps...a cooler easterly flow combined with broader coverage of 
clouds should keep highs generally in the lower 80s today. Despite 
the potential for scattered convection Saturday...southerly flow 
reestablishing will enable afternoon highs to recover into the mid 
and upper 80s with warmest temperatures in the Wabash Valley.

Sunday through Thursday 

Upper ridging centered over the southern Plains will expand 
northeast into the region Sunday into early next week with a 
transition back to a hotter and more humid airmass over central 
Indiana for the first half of next week. Highs will likely warm back 
into the lower and possibly mid 90s by Tuesday and Wednesday as the 
upper ridge centers over the Tennessee Valley. With a cold front 
stalled to the north over the Great Lakes...convective risks are 
minimal through Wednesday...isolated and diurnally driven at best.

The eastward progression of a stronger upper level wave diving out 
of the Pacific northwest is likely to be the catalyst that will 
finally suppress the upper ridge over the eastern part of the 
country and enable the cold front to shift south into the forecast 
area. Trends within the model suite however now suggest that will 
not take place until the second half of the next week with chances 
for showers and thunderstorms focusing on Thursday and Friday next 
week with temperatures cooling back to near seasonal levels by the 
end of next week. 

This will also now delay the arrival of our first taste of an early 
Fall airmass as the cold front departs to the southeast...with 
cooler than normal temperatures holding off until later next weekend 
into the early part of the following week.
